numerical_failure.observed_behavior: On ARM, float-to-int64 overflow saturates to INT64_MAX instead of wrapping to INT64_MIN. This makes the integer-shortcut condition misfire for out-of-bounds (OOB) float values like float(2**63), because np.float64(2**63) == np.int64(INT64_MAX) evaluates to True on ARM. The function then silently takes the integer shortcut rather than falling through to the vectorized OOB handling path.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: OOB float values should not satisfy the integer shortcut check; they should fall through to cast_from_unit_vectorized, which already has its own OOB check, and then handle the `errors` parameter correctly (including raising OutOfBoundsDatetime when errors == "raise").
trigger_conditions: Execution on ARM where float-to-int64 overflow saturates to INT64_MAX instead of wrapping
Input has dtype kind "f" (float) with OOB float values such as float(2**63)
The integer shortcut condition is evaluated using (arg == int_values) where int_values is arg.astype(np.int64), causing OOB floats to incorrectly compare equal due to saturation

input_output_examples.input: np.float64(2**63) (i.e., float(2**63)) in a float array passed to _to_datetime_with_unit with unit '{unit}'
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Silently produces incorrect datetime results by incorrectly taking the integer shortcut (no specific wrong datetime value provided in the passages).
input_output_examples.expected_output: Should not take the integer shortcut; should fall through to cast_from_unit_vectorized which performs its own OOB check and, when errors == "raise", raises OutOfBoundsDatetime("cannot convert input with unit '{unit}'").
input_output_examples.source: pr_body:PR#64643 summary and datetimes.py discussion showing misfire for float(2**63) and removal of OOB pre-check in favor of in_int64_range guard; discussion shows raise OutOfBoundsDatetime for OOB when errors == "raise"

oracle_clues: On ARM, np.float64(2**63) == np.int64(INT64_MAX) evaluates to True, incorrectly passing (arg == int_values)

The fix introduces an in_int64_range guard on the shortcut condition (exclude values outside the int64 domain) so OOB values fall through to cast_from_unit_vectorized which already has its own OOB check
When the (old) OOB pre-check found OOB values and errors == "raise", it raised OutOfBoundsDatetime(f"cannot convert input with unit '{unit}'")

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: OOB float value float(2**63) / int64 boundary (uses 2**63, int64 min/max)
category_specific_evidence: On ARM, float-to-int64 overflow saturates to INT64_MAX instead of wrapping to INT64_MIN (as on x86).
This caused the integer shortcut to misfire for OOB float values like float(2**63), because np.float64(2**63) == np.int64(INT64_MAX) evaluates to True on ARM.
Integer shortcut check must exclude values outside the int64 domain; fix adds an in_int64_range guard: in_int64_range = (arg >= np.float64(-(2**63))) & (arg < np.float64(2**63)) (datetimes path).

Timedelta path fix adds in_int64_range guard: in_int64_range = (data >= np.float64(i64.min)) & (data < np.float64(i64.max)) and changes all_round to all_round = (mask | (in_int64_range & (data == int_data))).all().

Test added to ensure OutOfBoundsTimedelta is raised for non-ns unit conversion using value = np.float64(2**63) in an array of dtype np.float64; with pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsTimedelta, match="cannot convert input"): to_timedelta(arr, unit="s").
The PR notes a latent bug in the timedelta path for non-ns units that this fix corrects.
reproduction_risks: Reproduction is architecture-dependent (ARM behavior differs from x86 regarding float-to-int64 overflow: saturation vs wrapping).
Reproduction depends on exercising the integer shortcut path (i.e., using float-to-int conversion for to_datetime/to_timedelta where the shortcut condition applies).
If the input is not OOB for int64 (e.g., not around float(2**63)), the reported shortcut misfire may not occur.
